I am 74, so I will not chase complicated or risky crops. I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation I know best, because in Quzhou this is the steadiest way for me to keep grain output, spread labor across the year, and avoid marketing trouble. I will use improved seed instead of expensive hybrid wheat, and hybrid seed for maize because maize responds better and gives me more stable yield. I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels, not too heavy, because inputs cost money and too much nitrogen can make the crop soft, lodge easily, and waste water. I will plough before wheat to keep the soil loose and store moisture, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow maize quickly. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat here needs water at key stages, while maize can usually manage with fewer turns if summer rain is normal. I will spray only as needed but I will not skip basic disease and insect control, because if I wait too long, the loss is bigger than the spray cost. This year I will keep things simple, familiar, and manageable with my strength.
